description: Builds a sixteen-note voicing from a root, taking its notes from one of twenty chord types laid out across nine octaves

params.text: Chooses the chord type from twenty, running from Power, Major and Minor through Quartal and Hendrix to Cluster, Ghost and The End; the tooltip and the display both name the one chosen
Sets how widely the sixteen notes are taken from the chord: below a third of its travel they are the sixteen nearest the root and above two thirds they are stretched across every octave it reaches
Shifts the window of notes up the chord in whole steps, 0 to 15, which rotates the voicing

inputs.text: The root the chord is built on, at 1V per octave
Adds to the chord type, two types per volt
Adds to the spread, a tenth of its range per volt
Adds to the inversion, one and a half steps per volt, wrapping back to 0 after 15

outputs.text: Sixteen channels of pitch, at 1V per octave

notes: the output always carries sixteen channels, whatever is patched.
the notes are taken only from the range -4V to 5V, and where the chord does not reach sixteen notes in that range the module adds notes an octave at a time above the last one.
the display names the chord and draws a mark for each of the sixteen voices across the nine octaves.
with the SPREAD knob between a third and two thirds of its travel the notes are taken from a span halfway between the two extremes.
the voicing is worked out again only when the root, type, spread, inversion or the shuffle changes, so a held chord costs almost nothing.
each of the three knobs draws a gold arc from its own position round to where its CV input has moved it.
menu: Scramble Channel Routing — shuffles which output channel carries which note of the voicing, so a polyphonic voice assigner gets the notes in a jumbled order

inputs.0: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.1:
stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
